tier_reason: Every quoted number matches site/data/results/agensio.json and the sibling nginx.json, zix.json, h2o.json and drogon.json in MDA2AV/HttpArena; the code is public (frameworks/agensio/{Dockerfile,agensio.toml,start.sh}, agensio src/handlers/httparena.cpp at v0.1.0-alpha.23, frameworks/nginx/{Dockerfile,nginx.conf,ngx_http_httparena_module.c}), the build flags are stated (CMake Release -march=native, nginx --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG' on debian:trixie GCC) and site/data/current.json names the Threadripper PRO 3995WX, so A on the HttpArena precedent (zix, nilo, dusty, actix).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: From frameworks/agensio/Dockerfile (agensio tag v0.1.0-alpha.23): debian:trixie with build-essential (GCC, version not pinned in the Dockerfile; Debian 13 ships GCC 14.2, which the agensio CLAUDE.md names), cmake -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DAGENSIO_TESTS=OFF -DAGENSIO_NATIVE=ON -DAGENSIO_HTTPARENA=ON, which adds -march=native; AGENSIO_HARDEN is on by default in CMakeLists.txt (-fstack-protector-strong, -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS, PIE with -z relro -z now), and CMake's Release default for GCC is -O3 -DNDEBUG (inferred). nginx entry: 1.31.4 on debian:trixie built with --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG', HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 modules, ngx_brotli and the custom ngx_http_httparena_module, linked against Debian trixie's OpenSSL from libssl-dev (the Dockerfile comment mentions quictls, but no step builds it).
corrections.caveats: Pre-alpha: the project started 2026-09-19 (CHANGELOG alpha.1), the README status line still reads 0.1.0-alpha.23 while tags have reached v0.1.0-alpha.72 (2026-10-12), and the README warns of unfound bugs, some possibly security bugs; post-alpha.23 releases fixed security issues found by the author's own audit (alpha.56: the HTTP/2 per-stream timeout check could stall a worker), none of which appears to change the measured request path. The HttpArena entry was submitted by the project author (meta.json maintainer YiannisBourkelis) and the committed numbers come from the alpha.23 build (frameworks/agensio/Dockerfile AGENSIO_REF=v0.1.0-alpha.23), while the repo has since moved on. In HttpArena the benchmark endpoints are a handler module compiled into each server, so the rows measure the server's request path on tiny canned responses, not real applications. JSON rows are not like-for-like: agensio's handler (src/handlers/httparena.cpp, load_httparena_dataset) pre-serializes every item's JSON except the total at dataset load and only appends prefixes and total*m per request, while nginx's ngx_http_httparena_module.c deliberately keeps typed fields and runs ngx_sprintf over every field per request; HttpArena's infrastructure rule for json-tls says the body must be serialized per request and no pre-serialized response cache qualifies, so the json-tls 1.31x and json-h2c 2.64x leads over nginx partly measure skipped serialization. On the h2 and h2c rows agensio, zix and h2o all land at 14-16M req/s while agensio uses 1.5-1.9k percent CPU against 3-4k for zix and h2o, so those rows look load-generator bound and the gap to zix and h2o is within noise; the CPU column is the better discriminator there, and nginx at 2.5-3.4M and about 6400% CPU is clearly server bound. nginx's config has no open_file_cache and 65536 worker_connections, which probably explains its 3.5GiB memory and part of the static-TLS gap against agensio's in-memory file cache (which revalidates by stat at most once a second; the infrastructure tier allows in-memory caching); nginx also offers TLS 1.3 only and links Debian trixie's OpenSSL (its Dockerfile comment mentions quictls but no step builds it). agensio was measured with its hardening defaults on (stack-protector-strong, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS, -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero, PIE and full RELRO), a cost nginx's -O3 -march=native build does not carry. agensio also loses to nginx on limited-conn, to h2o on baseline and baseline-h2, to zix on baseline-4096 and json-h2c, and to Drogon on pipelined. All servers here are typed 'infrastructure' (Drogon is 'flagship'). The agensio repo's own CLAUDE.md reports a CPU-per-request advantage over nginx on an M1 Pro (2026-09-15) and a Ryzen 9 9900X (2026-09-16, GCC 14.2, nginx 1.26.3, wrk 4.1), with result files committed under bench/results/ (for example 20260916-1951*.md); a few rows (10 MB streams, HTTPS 10 MB, HTTP 100 KB on macOS) favour nginx by the author's own table. Rows are the best of several runs per profile.

notes: All rps, CPU and memory figures for agensio, nginx, zix, h2o and Drogon check out against the HttpArena result JSONs; MIT, 1 star, 317 commits, last commit 2026-10-12, latest tag v0.1.0-alpha.72. Shortcomings: json-tls and json-h2c wins come partly from pre-serializing item JSON at load, against the profile's infrastructure rule and unlike nginx's per-request sprintf; h2/h2c rows look load-generator bound; numbers from alpha.23 while the project is at alpha.72; author-submitted entry; the record's claim that raw result files are absent was wrong (bench/results/ holds them).
